_doc: What each pinned source contributes to the atlas, DECLARED rather than inferred. A source absent from this file contributes nothing, and that is a decision someone made rather than a gap nobody noticed. `module` is the CLDF module the publisher declares in its own descriptor — dispatch follows their taxonomy, not our guess. `nullTokens` are the strings a source uses for 'no answer'; an undeclared token is a hard error rather than a value, because ingesting one writes 'we do not know' as though it were a fact. `parameterMap` maps the source's own parameter IDs onto ours; entries may be an object when the source stores JSON in its Value column, declaring which key to read and, where the source has no CodeTable, the closed vocabulary an unlisted value must fail against.

curated:method-coverage.contributes: which translation methods cover which languages
curated:method-coverage.note: OURS. Each entry is transcribed cite-only from a provider's own published language list, with the URL and the date read, so it pins to its own content hash and the commit that last changed it -- never under a provider's name, because Google did not tell us this, we read their page. Two entries (translated, omt1600) publish a headline count and NO enumeration; their counts are real and cannot become per-language facts, so they are skipped and the skip is reported.

curated:metric-coverage.contributes: which evaluation metric models cover which languages
curated:metric-coverage.note: OURS, transcribed cite-only from each model's own published list. AfriCOMET publishes language NAMES; the ISO 639-3 mapping is ours and the register says so. XLM-R is recorded as UNRESOLVED: its model card gives the count (100) and not the list, and transcribing an appendix by hand is how the previous register acquired a 'Top-100' note over a list of 77.

elcat.nullTokenNote: ELCat packs JSON into Value; a missing key reads as absent rather than as a token.

vitality.vocabularyNote: ELCat's own nine-level scale, which is NOT Glottolog AES's six. Declared here so a tenth level fails the build instead of arriving silently. 'awakening' and 'dormant' have no AES equivalent at all — which is why the two are separate Source_Scales rather than one merged vocabulary.

speakers.vocabularyNote: No vocabulary: ELCat publishes BANDS (1-9, 10-99, 100-999, 1000-9999, 10000-99999, 100000) plus the word 'Awakening'. Six of its seven forms are not numbers. Kept verbatim as a string — a midpoint would manufacture precision no source claims. 'Date Of Info' is FREE TEXT ('the 2002 census of the Russian Federation'), so it is preserved in Comment; parsing a year out of it would be a derivation and must not wear ELCat's name.

aes.scaleNote: Glottolog's Agglomerated Endangerment Status: six levels (not endangered, threatened, shifting, moribund, nearly extinct, extinct). This is NOT ELCat's nine-level scale — there is no AES equivalent of 'awakening' or 'dormant' — so the two are separate Source_Scales and a card showing both reports them as incommensurable rather than as a disagreement.

med.scaleNote: Most Extensive Description level: the ordinal is an index, the label (grammar, grammar sketch, wordlist, ...) is the fact.

grambank.nullTokenNote: '?' means the coder read the grammar and it does not answer. 79,638 rows — 18% of the dataset. It becomes not_attested, never the string '?'.

GB415.scaleNote: Grambank codes this BINARY: absent/present. WALS 45A codes the same question in four levels, so the two are separate Source_Scales and a card showing both reports them incommensurable.
